comment: M1–M9: Codes for the nine alkali-activated concrete mixtures. The paper screens M1–M6 as meeting the specified engineering requirements and excludes M7–M9; codes refer to mixture formulations, not assessment indicators.
ECO2: Name used by the authors for their combined environmental–economic assessment/index. Treat ECO2 as the study's framework name; its spelling alone does not justify inventing an expanded acronym.
Life-365: Service-life prediction software used for concrete durability modeling, particularly chloride-related deterioration; its output is modeled service life, not measured lifespan.
FA = fly ash; GGBS = ground-granulated blast-furnace slag. Mix IDs: M1 is the control; M2–M4 use 20%, 30% and 40% slag replacement; M5–M7 use 20%, 30% and 40% fly-ash replacement.
LCIA = Life Cycle Impact Assessment, the environmental impact-characterization phase of LCA. This article does not report a measured/computed LCIA inventory for its Sustainable Performance Index.
INR = Indian rupee. Figures in INR/m³ describe the authors' reported mixture material-cost comparisons, not a complete discounted life-cycle cost.

CML-IA = an environmental Life Cycle Impact Assessment method developed through Leiden University's Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML). GWP100a = global warming potential evaluated over 100 years; it is a climate-impact indicator, not a direct measured cooling-energy quantity.

B4: Spanish building/climate-zone code identifying a particular combination of winter and summer climatic severity. The cited cooling-load result is for the specified roof and B4 scenario, not every climate.

CTR = control cement façade panel without recycled textile nonwoven reinforcement. TW6L = cement composite with six layers of textile-waste nonwoven fabric. These labels identify the experimental panel alternatives.

MIVES indicator codes: I7 = acoustic performance, I8 = thermal performance, I9 = fire vulnerability. They are converted to value/satisfaction scores; they are not monetary costs or independent life-cycle impact categories.
RHA = rice husk ash, a supplementary cementitious material produced from rice husks. In this database study it may replace part of cement or sand, as specified by each mixture record.
LCC = life-cycle costing. The reported CEF calculation uses estimated constituent-material cost and compressive strength; it is not a comprehensive discounted LCC model.

MIVES = Integrated Value Model for Sustainability Assessment. The authors transform 18 indicators through satisfaction functions and aggregate seven criteria using requirement weights: 29% economic, 39% environmental and 32% social. Social scoring here is not a separate S-LCA.
HOT2000: Canadian building energy simulation software used to estimate residential energy demand. These are simulated operating-energy inputs, distinct from observed whole-life performance.

A1–C4: Building life-cycle module codes spanning product, construction, use and end-of-life stages. A1 begins with raw-material supply; C4 represents final disposal. The paper compares modeled impacts and costs over a 60-year scenario.
GHG = greenhouse gases, commonly reported as CO₂-equivalent emissions. ODP = ozone depletion potential, a separate environmental impact category; lower GHG emissions do not guarantee lower ODP.

MPa = megapascal (10⁶ pascals), a unit of stress/strength. The paper's author-labeled 'durability' value expressed in MPa is a mechanical-performance proxy, not an experimental measurement of service life.

SHAP = SHapley Additive exPlanations (feature attribution for model predictions). GPR = Gaussian Process Regression (probabilistic regression with predictive uncertainty). PPO = Proximal Policy Optimization (reinforcement-learning optimization). In this paper these are reported computational methods, not independently verified field results.

Wiener stochastic degradation model: A probability-based model representing deterioration as a random process over time. Here it is used to model freeze–thaw degradation/reliability separately from the mixture's embodied energy, carbon and cost calculations.

SimaPro = software for environmental Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). Ecoinvent 3 = background life-cycle inventory database. ReCiPe 2016 = life-cycle impact-characterization method. Midpoint indicators address impact mechanisms/categories; endpoint indicators estimate aggregated damage to human health, ecosystems and resources; these are environmental, not standalone social LCA, outcomes.

GEMIS = environmental modeling tool used for life-cycle energy/emissions comparisons. Its results should be compared with SimaPro only when the reported impact definitions, denominators and units are genuinely equivalent.
M1–M9: Codes for the nine alkali-activated concrete mixtures. The paper's screening accepts M1–M6 under its engineering thresholds; M7–M9 are excluded.

ECO2: The study's environmental–economic sustainability assessment framework/index, combining performance and burden measures. Do not assume that the framework name has an unstated official acronym expansion.
IITPave: Pavement structural-design software used for mechanistic-empirical evaluation of the required pavement layers under subgrade and traffic conditions.
Life-365: Concrete service-life prediction software, principally for chloride-related deterioration; its forecast does not establish experimentally observed service life.
INR = Indian rupee. The quoted amounts are mixture material-cost comparisons per m³; they should not be interpreted as whole-life discounted costs.
FA = fly ash; GGBS = ground-granulated blast-furnace slag. M1 = control; M2–M4 = 20%, 30%, 40% slag replacement; M5–M7 = 20%, 30%, 40% fly-ash replacement.
LCIA = Life Cycle Impact Assessment (environmental impact characterization). Binder intensity is a resource-use proxy, not an author-reported measured LCIA category.
WG1 = recycled soda-lime-silica glass; WG2 = recycled lead-silicate glass recovered from discarded cathode-ray-tube televisions. These codes identify alternative roof-tile coatings.
CML-IA: Life-cycle environmental impact characterization method associated with Leiden University's Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML); not building-energy simulation software.
GWP100a = global warming potential over 100 years. B4 identifies a specific Spanish climate zone. The reported cooling saving is scenario-specific and should not be assumed in other climate zones.
TW6L = experimental cement panel with six layers of recycled textile-waste nonwoven fabric; CTR = the unreinforced control cement panel.
MIVES comfort/fire assessment indicators: I7 = acoustic response; I8 = thermal response; I9 = fire vulnerability. Indicator satisfaction is scored and weighted in the MIVES hierarchy.

S-LCA = Social Life Cycle Assessment. The authors use social/comfort indicators within a multicriteria sustainability model; this does not establish a separately implemented, full Social Life Cycle Assessment.
RHA = rice husk ash, a supplementary cementitious material derived from rice husks; the study separates concrete mixtures according to how much ash replaces cement or sand.

LCA = Life Cycle Assessment; LCC = Life Cycle Costing. This paper calculates material-emissions and material-cost efficiency using published strength data; it does not perform complete LCA and LCC across every life-cycle stage.

MIVES = Integrated Value Model for Sustainability Assessment, using weighted satisfaction/value functions. Delphi = structured, iterative expert consultation for developing/refining judgments and weights. The study's economic/environmental/social requirement weights are 29%/39%/32%.

HOT2000 = Canadian residential building energy simulation software. A1–C4 = building life-cycle modules from raw-material supply through end-of-life disposal; the paper examines a 60-year life-cycle scenario.
GHG = greenhouse gases. ODP = ozone depletion potential, a distinct LCIA indicator. Modeled GHG and energy reductions do not imply improvements in ozone depletion.

SHAP = SHapley Additive exPlanations; GPR = Gaussian Process Regression; PPO = Proximal Policy Optimization. The article describes feature interpretation, probabilistic inventory prediction and reinforcement-learning optimization. Its internal source inconsistencies and validation limitations remain unresolved.

MPa = megapascal, a unit of stress/strength. MPa cannot directly express observed service life or long-term durability; the article's MPa-valued 'durability' claim should be understood as a mechanical-performance proxy.

Wiener stochastic model: Probability-based time-evolution model for random degradation. The authors use it for freeze–thaw reliability/service prediction, distinct from the embodied-carbon/energy inventory calculation.

SimaPro = Life Cycle Assessment modeling software. Ecoinvent 3 = source of background inventory factors. ReCiPe 2016 = life-cycle impact-characterization method with environmental midpoint and endpoint indicators.

Midpoint indicators quantify environmental impact mechanisms/categories; endpoint indicators aggregate damage consequences for human health, ecosystems and resource scarcity. Environmental human-health damage is not by itself Social Life Cycle Assessment.

GEMIS = emissions/energy modeling software. Cross-software comparison with SimaPro is meaningful only for equivalent impact definitions and units; the article's ozone indicators are not necessarily directly comparable.
SDGs = United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The authors' SDG links are qualitative; this study does not quantify achievement of a specific SDG target.
